negativeCorpus.reason: `preserves` takes a one-state invariant and `attempt immutability` is a two-state relation. Immutability is not an invariant of a single state, and the categories keep the two apart

negativeCorpus.reason: `depends only on` takes a state projection on the right and a state-relative relation on the left. `ancestry` is a relation, not a projection, so the two positions are not interchangeable
negativeCorpus.sentence: ancestry depends only on ancestry

negativeCorpus.reason: an unlifted payload condition. `the parent count equals two` is a condition on a commit, and `requires` needs a condition on the transition's label, so the label match cannot be left implicit
negativeCorpus.sentence: every merge append requires the parent count equals two

negativeCorpus.reason: three-way ordinary `or` coordination. `or` is binary, so a three-term list has a left and a right reading. No list construct or final `or` coordinator ships, so rather than pick an association the grammar refuses the sentence. The separately typed `and additionally` form is available only for explicit three-sentence conjunctions
negativeCorpus.sentence: every content resolve requires a home tenant or a granted tenant or a home tenant for the resolved reference

negativeCorpus.reason: the same defect at sentence level. Conjunction is associative in meaning, which is exactly why the grammar must not silently choose: an ambiguity it tolerates here is one it would tolerate where association changes the reading
negativeCorpus.sentence: every effect step preserves disjoint receipt ids and every effect step preserves disjoint receipt ids and every effect step preserves disjoint receipt ids

negativeCorpus.reason: the nearby misreading of the custody sentence. `maintains` takes a two-state relation and `carrier refs only` is a one-state invariant, so reading the ref-only rule as a relation between the states either side of a step is refused rather than silently accepted as the invariant it is not
negativeCorpus.sentence: every secret step maintains carrier refs only

negativeCorpus.reason: the converse nearby misreading. `preserves` takes a one-state invariant and `an unowned reference` is a condition on a state and a payload, so a precondition cannot be smuggled in as an invariant
negativeCorpus.sentence: every content step preserves an unowned reference

negativeCorpus.reason: the ontology refuses it. `is transitive` takes a binary relation over one type; a transition family is a relation over a state, a label, and a state, and the two are not interchangeable however similar the English reads
negativeCorpus.sentence: every secret step is transitive

negativeCorpus.reason: the label match is not optional in the other direction either. Lifting a firing-payload condition under the firing label yields a condition, not a two-state relation, so `maintains` refuses it
negativeCorpus.sentence: every routing step maintains an unconsumed event key for the firing

negativeCorpus.reason: an unlifted payload condition, on a second domain. `a passed destination` is a relation over a Binding and a destination, and `requires` needs a condition on the transition's label, so the egress label match cannot be left implicit
negativeCorpus.sentence: every isolate egress requires a passed destination

negativeCorpus.reason: the same defect for a session-scoped use: the condition ranges over a SessionUse and the transition over an EnvironmentLabel, so the use projection cannot be left implicit
negativeCorpus.sentence: every environment step requires a live current session

negativeCorpus.reason: the same defect once more, and the reason the lifter is a separate entry rather than a match inside the condition's own denotation
negativeCorpus.sentence: every template materialization requires an unmaterialized template

negativeCorpus.reason: the model refuses a grammatical sentence. `a home tenant` is a relation over a ContentLedger, a ContentRef, and a Tenant; the resolved-secret lifter wants one over a SecretLedger, a SecretRef, and a Tenant. Two custody rules that read almost identically in English are kept apart by the ledger they range over
negativeCorpus.sentence: every secret resolve requires a home tenant for the resolved secret

negativeCorpus.reason: two lifters of one domain are not interchangeable. The resolved-reference lifter scopes a reference-and-Tenant relation under a resolve label; `an unowned reference` is a condition on a reference alone, so pairing them is refused
negativeCorpus.sentence: every content collect requires an unowned reference for the resolved reference

negativeCorpus.reason: a lifted condition is not a sentence. Without a transition family there is nothing for the bound to be a bound of, and the grammar has no way to supply the missing quantifier
negativeCorpus.sentence: the parent count is at most two for the appended commit

negativeCorpus.reason: a relation is not a quantity. `is at most` compares two quantities read off a source state and a label, and an order over contributions is neither
negativeCorpus.sentence: interceptor ordering is at most two

negativeCorpus.reason: coordination at the wrong level. Sentence-level `and` takes a sentence on each side, and `recorded entry immutability` is a two-state relation. Conjoining the two invariants would need coordination at the relation level, which the grammar does not have and which this corpus therefore does not report
negativeCorpus.sentence: every audit step maintains a typed lower local cause and recorded entry immutability

negativeCorpus.reason: the fresh-state family cannot recover the egress payload. `a passed destination` is a Binding-and-Destination relation, while `requires` needs a condition on the IsolateLabel; the egress lifter remains necessary even when the source state is known exactly
negativeCorpus.sentence: every fresh isolate step requires a passed destination

negativeCorpus.reason: a functional state-relative mapping is not a binary relation over one domain. `is transitive` takes `PR`, whereas an approval lookup is `RE` over a ledger, an InvocationId, and an ApprovalId
negativeCorpus.sentence: approval mapping is transitive

negativeCorpus.reason: the duplicate write id cannot be left implicit. `a recorded original reply` is a payload-indexed postcondition, while `establishes` needs a postcondition on the SubmissionLabel; the `for the duplicate` lifter is what ties that id to the resubmit label
negativeCorpus.sentence: every duplicate submission establishes a recorded original reply

negativeCorpus.reason: the same post-state payload rule on a second label family. `disposed child facets` is indexed by the SessionId a close label carries; without `for the closed session`, the grammar refuses the missing label-to-payload binding
negativeCorpus.sentence: every session close establishes disposed child facets

negativeCorpus.reason: `PO` is deliberately distinct from `TR` despite sharing its Lean type. A transition family says which steps exist; a postcondition says what those steps establish. Letting the former stand in for the latter would make the new grammar form tautological, so the category mismatch is refused
negativeCorpus.sentence: every duplicate submission establishes every duplicate submission
